title: The wrong platform
focus: Natural questions, contrast, reassurance, two stable speakers and turn transitions.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: You look worried. Did we miss the train?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: I don't think so. The screen says platform thirteen, but my ticket says thirty. That can't be right, can it?

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Let me see. Oh, that's the seat number. We're in carriage two, seats thirty and thirty-one.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Right. So we need platform thirteen, not platform thirty. I was about to run to the other end of the station.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: We've still got twelve minutes. Shall I carry your bag?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Would you? Thanks. It's heavier than it looks. I packed a few books.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: A few? Are we going away for a weekend or opening a library?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Very funny. Come on, then. We can argue about my books on the train.

title: A small change to my mornings
focus: Clear learner-friendly narration, connected speech, sentence stress and pacing without a style prompt.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Last month, I decided to stop checking my phone before breakfast. At first, it felt strange. What if I missed an important message? What if something happened at work? But most mornings, nothing urgent had happened at all. I was simply reading the news and making myself anxious. Now I leave my phone in the kitchen overnight. When I wake up, I open the curtains, make some tea, and sit by the window for ten minutes. Sometimes I read a page of a book. Sometimes I just watch the street. It hasn't changed my whole life. I still get tired, and I still spend too much time online. But my mornings feel a little quieter. The surprising part is that I don't need more time. I just need to choose what gets my attention first.

title: Numbers, word stress and difficult sounds
focus: Thirteen versus thirty, word-class stress, consonant clusters, dates and natural punctuation. Listen for omissions or altered words.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Thirteen tickets. Thirty tickets. I ordered thirteen, not thirty. Please record the meeting. Keep a record of the meeting. I present the results. It's a birthday present. She thought the three thin threads were thicker than these. The sixth guest left her clothes beside the desk. We used to work together, but we're used to working alone now. The appointment is on Thursday, the twenty-first of January, at a quarter past three. Does that work for you? Actually, could we make it half past three instead?

title: The repair cafe
focus: Longer two-speaker consistency, a developing story, pauses and meaning-driven prosody.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Do you remember that little radio I found at my grandmother's house? The green one with the broken handle? I finally took it to the repair cafe on Saturday.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: A repair cafe? I thought that was just a place to get coffee while someone fixed your bike.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: That's what I thought too. But it's a room in the community centre. People bring things that don't work, and volunteers help them repair them. You don't just leave your things at the door. You sit down and help.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That sounds useful. Did they manage to fix the radio?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Not immediately. A man called Peter asked me when it had last worked. I said I had no idea. Then he asked whether I'd tried new batteries. I felt a bit silly, because I hadn't.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Don't tell me it only needed batteries.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: No, the batteries weren't the problem. One of the small metal parts inside was loose. Peter showed me how to clean it and put it back. He could have done it in two minutes, but he let me do it myself.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Were you nervous? I'd be afraid of breaking something else.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: A little. My hands were shaking when I picked up the tiny screwdriver. But Peter said, 'It's already broken. Let's see what we can learn.' That made me relax.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: And then it worked?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Yes! First there was a horrible noise, and then we heard a weather forecast. Everyone at our table stopped talking. I don't think anyone has ever been so pleased to hear that rain was expected on Sunday.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: I love that. How much did they charge you?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Nothing. There was a box for donations, so I put some money in. They asked me to come back next month, even if I didn't have anything to repair.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Maybe I'll come with you. I've got a lamp that hasn't worked for years. And yes, before you ask, I've already changed the bulb.
